summary: Isaiah 65 (25 verses) continues the story of holiness. Starting with '“I am inquired of by those who didn’t ask. I am found by those who didn’t seek me. I said, ‘See me, see me,’ to a nation that was not called by my name.', it moves through themes of holiness, judgment and calls readers toward hope.
whyItMatters: This chapter matters because it shows holiness lived out in assyrian crisis, exile hope. For a first-time reader, it answers: who is God in this moment, what does he ask, and how do people respond.

keyVerses.text: “I am inquired of by those who didn’t ask. I am found by those who didn’t seek me. I said, ‘See me, see me,’ to a nation that was not called by my name.

Therefore the Lord Yahweh says, “Behold, my servants will eat, but you will be hungry; behold, my servants will drink, but you will be thirsty. Behold, my servants will rejoice, but you will be disapp
The wolf and the lamb will feed together. The lion will eat straw like the ox. Dust will be the serpent’s food. They will not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain,” says Yahweh.

questions.answer: In 25 verses, this chapter isaiah 65 (25 verses) continues the story of holiness. starting with '“i am inquired of by those who didn’t ask. i am found by those who didn’t seek me. i said, ‘see me, see me,’ to a nation that was not called by my name.', it moves through themes of holiness, judgment and calls readers toward hope. The setting is assyrian crisis, exile hope, written to judah. Look for who speaks, who listens, and what changes by the end.

questions.question: Who wrote Isaiah and why 65 matters in the bigger story?
questions.answer: Traditionally isaiah son of amoz, addressed to judah around ~700 bc. This chapter fits the book's purpose as prophecy — its themes of holiness, judgment build on what came before.

questions.question: Are there any difficult words here?
questions.answer: Scan for names, places, or repeated abstract words like righteousness, covenant, or glory. The glossary below defines up to 3 that show up most. Ask: who is this person, what does this word mean in everyday terms?

questions.question: What does this chapter teach about God or people?
questions.answer: Through holiness and judgment, it shows God's character (faithful, just, merciful) and human tendency (need, failure, hope). Notice how verses move from problem to provision.

questions.question: Verse 12 is long — what is it saying in plain English?
questions.answer: The verse says: 'I will destine you to the sword, and you will all bow down to the slaughter; because when I called, you didn’t answer. When I spoke, you didn’t listen; but you did that which was e...' In plain terms: it is making a key point about holiness. Break it into two halves — what is described, and what is promised or commanded.

questions.question: How could this chapter apply today without forcing modern ideas onto it?
questions.answer: Ask: what was original audience supposed to do with this? Then ask: what similar situation exists today? For example, if chapter warns about idols, today that might be money or status; if it celebrates deliverance, where do people need deliverance today?
